correctness.rationale: For every positive input length the fair-input pair split gives independent uniform u and conditional uniform v, proving an exact binomial recursion including odd remainders. The nonstandard binomial concavity deficit is bounded uniformly below 4 by a complete two-region Taylor/Chernoff estimate; both global power-law barriers then follow by strong induction, accounting for the zero-child binomial atom. The expected residual-one identity follows by an exact second recursion. Independent direct enumeration through length 12, exact rational recurrences through length 90, and the saved verifier support the algebra but are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The October 2026 primary paper prints the same fair-input residual recursion, identifies the golden-ratio exponent as a heuristic for the mean, and leaves the associated maximum-weight growth problem open; it does not establish the all-length two-sided mean power law. The present quantitative binomial Jensen-gap lemma and two strong inductions supply that missing proof. The 1992 and 2018 sources concern extraction rates, general recursion, or distinct conditional maximum-redundancy measures. Mathematical-record and literature searches found no statement implying the sharp mean exponent; some prior work may remain unindexed.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper specifically treats the exponent the base-two logarithm of the golden ratio as a heuristic for the fair residual mean while establishing only a larger deterministic upper exponent for maximum residual ones. The result proves the sharp polynomial order of the mean residual length, supplying two-sided absolute constants for all positive lengths and a necessary exponent barrier for maximum residual weight; this characterizes a natural information-loss invariant, not an arbitrary data-table increment. The remaining maximum-case question is explicitly not claimed.
